summary: The over-the-sink adjustable 2-tier dish drying rack is a deep, multi-retailer category - Walmart, Target, Wayfair and Amazon each carry several named SKUs (Costway, Skonyon, Sakugi, WLRETMCI, PremiumRacks, OXO and others) - but despite ten dedicated WebSearch queries across all four retailers (in addition to discovery's own earlier attempt), no exact per-unit price for any specific SKU could be confirmed from returned snippet text; only Amazon's category price-filter buckets ($15-30/$30-40/$40-60) are available, carried over from discovery as a low-confidence estimate. This agent could not satisfy the 'three competitors with confirmed prices' bar and is reporting status partial. Complaint evidence is stronger: recurring themes are structural wobble, rust (including rust on arrival), poor drainboard slope causing standing water, and damaged/mis-packed units on arrival. All evidence is WebSearch-snippet text; the underlying commerce domains are blocked at the environment's network proxy for direct page reads.

facts.claim: Walmart's own dish-rack browse category lists at least eight distinct over-the-sink adjustable 2-tier SKUs (Costway, WLRETMCI, OLOV, Sakugi and others), indicating a broad, competitive in-category catalogue at that one retailer alone.
Target separately lists Skonyon, Costway, WhizMax and Cheer Collection adjustable over-sink dish rack models.
Wayfair's over-the-sink dish rack category includes adjustable models spanning a 13.7-inch to 39.4-inch fit range across multiple SKUs.
Amazon carries PremiumRacks (multiple SKUs) and OXO Good Grips rustproof aluminum racks in this category, among others.
A recurring structural complaint is that the assembled rack wobbles so much it becomes unusable.
A recurring complaint is rust developing on the rack, in some cases appearing on parts (e.g. the flatware caddy) even on a newly arrived unit, and in other cases after roughly two years of use.
A recurring complaint is that the drainboard is not sloped enough, so water pools at the edges rather than draining into the sink.
At least one reviewer reported a unit arriving damaged, with mismatched parts (two left sides instead of a matching pair) and missing hardware that prevented assembly.

differentiation.angle: Silicone-capped, wide-set support feet marketed as 'won't scratch or slide in your sink', shown in a close-up placement demo
differentiation.rationale: Addresses the scratch/slip concern; testable in content only once the sourced unit's foot design is confirmed to match the claim.

differentiation.angle: 304/316 marine-grade stainless construction (not powder-coated steel) with an explicit rust-back guarantee
differentiation.rationale: Directly answers the rust complaint, including rust-on-arrival reports, which points to a base-material or coating issue rather than a use issue; needs a different material spec and a warranty policy from the supplier.
